text:
If you’re heading out for the last light, plan on a cool, breezy sunset around 7:05, with the northwest wind still noticeable before easing tonight. Skies clear out, and temperatures slip to about 45, so bring a layer for any lingering waterfront plans. On the lake, waves stay around 1 to 2 feet this evening before the wind goes light.

Tuesday starts quietly, then turns breezier under partly sunny skies. The forecast calls for a high near 70, though the models are split, with some keeping us in the mid 60s, so I’d dress for a seasonable day rather than summer warmth. South winds may gust to 24 mph, with lake waves building toward 1 to 3 feet. A shower is possible late Tuesday night, mainly after 2am. Enjoy the clear evening, and be ready for a jacket and a choppier lake by Tuesday afternoon.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): A warm front approaching the region Thursday brings increasing clouds and a 50% chance of light, stratiform rain showers through Thursday night, with high temperatures reaching the mid-70s. High pressure shifts across Quebec on Friday, bringing a refreshing north breeze, mostly sunny skies, and pleasant highs near 70° before lows drop into the upper 40s Friday night. An approaching weather system brings a cool and showery weekend pattern across Vermont and the North Country. Saturday features partly sunny skies with highs near 67° and scattered showers developing (40% chance), turning into widespread light rain on Sunday (60% chance) with highs held in the mid-60s. Lingering showers continue into next Monday with highs remaining cool in the mid-60s.
